title: Visual Correspondence Hallucination

en.text: Establishing correspondences between two overlapping images is a foundational step in computer vision, underpinning everything from visual localization to 3D reconstruction. Yet both classical and deep local-feature matchers share an unspoken assumption: a keypoint can only be “matched” if it is visible in both images. The moment it is hidden behind foreground clutter, or simply falls outside the field of view of the second image, these methods have nothing to say and quietly discard those regions as noise.

That assumption is exactly where things break down. Modern localization leans on keypoint matches, and when two images share little overlap, most points are either occluded or out of frame, so matching collapses. Humans do not give up so easily. Faced with a point they cannot see, people reason about the geometry of the scene and infer where the match ought to be. Classical vision uses geometric reasoning too, but almost always after the fact, wielding models like epipolar geometry to reject bad matches. No prior method actually predicts correspondences at locations that are not covisible across the two views.

This ICLR 2022 paper goes straight at that gap. The authors introduce the task of visual correspondence hallucination, along with a network called NeurHal. Given a pair of overlapping source and target images and a set of keypoints in the source, NeurHal outputs, for every keypoint, a probability distribution over its correspondent’s location in the target image — whether that location is visible, occluded, or entirely beyond the target frame.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three flavors of correspondence hallucination. The top row shows source images with a small set of keypoints; the bottom row shows the probability distributions NeurHal predicts in the target image. A red circle marks a visible correspondent that can simply be identified, a red plus marks an occluded point that must be inpainted, and a red cross marks a point beyond the target’s borders that must be outpainted. All three pairs come from scenes unseen during training.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09711 (arXiv:2106.09711, ICLR 2022). Authors: Hugo Germain, Vincent Lepetit, and Guillaume Bourmaud.
When matching runs out of pixels

It helps to break the problem into three sub-tasks, which the authors name explicitly: identifying (the correspondent is visible in the target), inpainting (the correspondent is occluded by foreground), and outpainting (the correspondent lies outside the target’s field of view). Conventional matchers can only ever handle the first, because they search for the most similar descriptor within the target’s pixel grid: an occluded point has no matching appearance, and an out-of-frame point is not even inside the search region.

NeurHal aims to solve all three with a single network. It is trained on the indoor dataset ScanNet and also tested on NYU Depth; outdoors, it is trained on MegaDepth and tested on ETH-3D. Crucially, every evaluation uses scenes never seen during training, so the numbers measure genuine generalization rather than memorization of the training environments.
How NeurHal hallucinates
The architecture reads left to right in Figure 2, from the two input images to a set of per-keypoint correspondence maps.

en.caption: Figure 2. Overview of NeurHal. On the left, a siamese backbone turns the source and target images into dense descriptor maps (the target map is padded outward with a learnable vector λ). A cross-attention backbone in the middle lets the two communicate, and on the right each keypoint feature is convolved over the target features and passed through a 2D softmax to yield a correspondence map.

en.text: In detail, a siamese convolutional backbone first encodes both images into dense descriptor maps. To give locations beyond the frame something to match against, the target descriptor map is padded outward with a learnable vector λ, effectively initializing descriptors past the image borders. A cross-attention backbone with positional encoding then lets the source and target descriptors exchange information — and this is precisely what allows the network to produce peaked distributions for occluded and out-of-frame points. Finally, each keypoint’s feature is convolved over the target features with a 1×1 convolution and passed through a 2D softmax to produce one correspondence map.

Training simply minimizes a sum of Neural Reprojection Error (NRE) terms — the negative log-likelihood of the true reprojected location — optimized with SGD and early stopping. The procedure assumes nothing about visibility and needs no labels marking points as visible, occluded, or out of frame; the network only ever emits correspondence maps. To emphasize geometry over texture detail, the maps are kept deliberately low-resolution: with an effective stride of 8 and an output ratio γ=50%, a 640×480 target yields a 160×120 map.
Can it really imagine the match?

The paper’s first research question is whether NeurHal can genuinely hallucinate unseen correspondents on scenes it never trained on. The capability table below gives a qualitative answer — the paper quantifies this with precision curves; here we only ask what each method can and cannot do.

en.caption: Table 1. What NeurHal and mainstream local-feature matchers can do on the three correspondence tasks.

en.text: The pattern is clear. Everyone can identify visible points; on inpainting, methods like LoFTR, DRC-Net, and S2DNet are weak; and on outpainting they fail almost entirely — because they only ever search inside the target’s borders and never place a correspondent beyond the frame. NeurHal, by contrast, produces predictions concentrated near the true location in all three cases. Figure 5 shows this ability directly on image pairs from scenes held out at training time.

en.caption: Figure 5. Qualitative inpainting and outpainting results. The top row shows outpainting examples, the bottom row inpainting examples. Each group runs, left to right: the source image with a keypoint (red dot), the target image, and the (negative-log) correspondence map predicted by NeurHal; the dashed blue rectangle marks the target’s true borders and the red circle marks the ground-truth correspondent. Even when the answer lies outside the frame, the probability mass concentrates on the correct side of the border.

en.text: Hallucinating matches makes camera pose more robust

What is this ability good for? The authors wire it into absolute camera pose estimation, a linchpin of visual localization. On 2500 held-out ScanNet source/target pairs, they measure how often the pose is estimated correctly (rotation error < 20°, translation error < 1.5 m) as a function of the image pair’s visual overlap.

en.caption: Figure 7. Absolute camera pose experiment on ScanNet. The horizontal axis is the maximum visual overlap of an image pair; the vertical axis is the fraction of poses estimated correctly. The green curve is NeurHal, sitting well above every competing local-feature matcher — especially in the hard, low-overlap regime where most correspondents are not visible.

en.text: The gap is widest exactly where the two images barely overlap and most correspondents fall outside the field of view — and NeurHal is the only method able to outpaint those points. In other words, the ability to imagine correspondents beyond the frame is what decides success on low-overlap pairs.
Which task actually does the work
So which of the three tasks buys this robustness? An ablation on ScanNet isolates the contribution of identifying, inpainting, and outpainting one at a time.

en.caption: Figure 6. Ablation on ScanNet. The dark curve is the full NeurHal trained on all three tasks — identifying, inpainting, and outpainting. Dropping the outpainting task (the lighter curves) clearly lowers pose accuracy in the low-overlap regime, whereas adding inpainting contributes far less.

en.text: The verdict: training on all three tasks together works best, and the outpainting task is what actually opens the gap — in low-overlap scenes, where most correspondents fall outside the frame, it very nearly decides the outcome. Adding inpainting, by contrast, brings only a modest extra benefit to pose estimation. That squares with intuition: the harder the low-overlap case, the more you need to place correspondents beyond the visible image.
Takeaway and boundaries

The message is simple but powerful: a single network can learn to hallucinate keypoint correspondences — visible, occluded, or entirely out of frame — and that ability makes absolute camera pose estimation markedly more robust on low-overlap image pairs. Put differently, NeurHal reframes non-covisible regions not as noise to be thrown away but as signal to be predicted through learned geometric reasoning.

It is worth being honest about the limits. NeurHal outputs deliberately low-resolution distributions that favor geometrically plausible location over pixel-level precision, and outpainted points still carry substantial uncertainty — often the model can only push the probability mass to the correct region. But as a first step toward turning correspondence hallucination into a learnable task in its own right, it makes the case cleanly: teaching a network to imagine what it cannot see is worth doing.

zh.text: 在两张有重叠的图片之间找到对应点，是从视觉定位到三维重建的基础一步。但无论是传统方法还是深度局部特征匹配，都有一个隐含前提：一个关键点只有在两张图里都看得见，才谈得上“匹配”。一旦它被前景挡住，或者干脆落在第二张图的画面之外，这些方法就无话可说，只能把这些区域当作噪声丢掉。
问题在于，现代视觉定位恰恰依赖这些关键点匹配，而当两张图片的重叠很少时，绝大多数点都处于被遮挡或视野之外的状态，匹配随之崩溃。人类却不会就此放弃：面对一个看不见的点，我们会根据场景的几何结构去推断它“应该”落在哪里。经典视觉里当然也有几何推理，但通常只用在事后，用对极几何这类模型去剔除错误匹配，从没有人真正去主动预测那些不可见位置上的对应点。
这篇发表于 ICLR 2022 的论文，正是冲着这个空白去的。作者提出“视觉对应幻想”（visual correspondence hallucination）这一新任务，以及一个名为 NeurHal 的网络：给定一对有重叠的源图与目标图，以及源图中的一批关键点，NeurHal 为每个关键点输出它的对应点在目标图上位置的概率分布——无论这个位置是可见、被遮挡，还是落在视野之外。

zh.caption: 图1 视觉对应幻想的三种情形。上排是源图及其上标出的少量关键点，下排是目标图上 NeurHal 预测的概率分布。红圈表示可以直接识别的可见对应点，红十字为需要“内补”的被遮挡点，红叉为需要“外补”、落在目标图边界之外的点。三组示例都来自训练时未见过的场景。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09711 （arXiv:2106.09711，ICLR 2022）。作者：Hugo Germain、Vincent Lepetit、Guillaume Bourmaud。
当匹配“看不见”时
要理解这项工作，先把对应点的定位拆成三个子任务。作者把它们统一命名为：识别（identifying，对应点在目标图里可见）、内补（inpainting，对应点被前景遮挡）、外补（outpainting，对应点落在目标图视野之外）。传统匹配方法天生只能处理第一种，因为它们只在目标图的像素范围内寻找最相似的描述子：被遮挡的点没有可匹配的外观，视野之外的点根本不在搜索范围里。
NeurHal 的目标，是用同一个网络把这三种情形一并解决。它在室内场景 ScanNet 上训练、并在 NYU Depth 上测试；在室外场景 MegaDepth 上训练、在 ETH-3D 上测试。关键在于，所有评测都使用训练时从未见过的场景，因此结果衡量的是真正的泛化能力，而不是对训练场景的记忆。
NeurHal 是怎么“脑补”的
NeurHal 的结构可以顺着图2 从左到右看：从两张输入图，到一组每个关键点各自的对应图。

zh.caption: 图2 NeurHal 总览。左侧为源图与目标图经孪生骨干得到的描述子图（目标图用可学习向量 λ 向外扩充），中间的交叉注意力骨干让二者互相“交流”，右侧每个关键点特征经 1×1 卷积与二维 softmax，得到一张对应图。

zh.text: 具体来说，一个孪生（siamese）卷积骨干网络先把源图和目标图各自编码成稠密的描述子图。为了让“视野之外”也有对应的描述子，目标图的描述子图会用一个可学习的向量 λ 向外扩充（padding），相当于为画面边界之外的位置预置了初始描述子。接着，一个带位置编码的交叉注意力（cross-attention）骨干让源图与目标图的描述子互相“交流”——这正是网络能为被遮挡和视野之外的点给出集中概率分布的关键。最后，每个关键点的特征以 1×1 卷积的方式扫过目标特征，再经过二维 softmax，得到一张对应图。

训练只需最小化一组神经重投影误差（Neural Reprojection Error，NRE）之和，也就是真实重投影位置的负对数似然，用 SGD 优化并配合早停。整个过程既不假设任何点可见，也不需要标注哪些点是可见、被遮挡还是视野之外——网络自始至终只输出对应图。为了突出几何而非纹理细节，对应图刻意保持低分辨率：在有效 stride 为 8、输出比例 γ=50% 时，一张 640×480 的目标图对应一张 160×120 的对应图。
它真的能“想象”出对应点吗
论文的第一个核心问题是：在没见过的场景里，NeurHal 能不能真正幻想出看不见的对应点？下面这张能力对比表先给出一个定性的回答——原文用精度曲线做了量化，这里只关心“能不能做到”。

zh.caption: 表1 NeurHal 与主流局部特征匹配方法在三类对应任务上的能力对比。

zh.text: 结论很直接：在识别可见点上，大家都能做；但在内补上，LoFTR、DRC-Net、S2DNet 等方法表现很弱；而在外补上它们几乎完全失效——因为这些方法只会在目标图边界以内搜索，根本不会把对应点放到画面之外。NeurHal 则在三种情形下都能给出集中在真实位置附近的预测。图5 用几组训练时未见过的图片，把这种能力直观地展示了出来。

zh.caption: 图5 定性的内补/外补结果。上排为外补示例，下排为内补示例。每组从左到右依次是：带关键点（红点）的源图、目标图，以及 NeurHal 预测的（负对数）对应图；蓝色虚线框标出目标图的真实边界，红圈为真实对应点。可以看到，即便正确答案落在边界之外，概率质量也能集中到框外正确的一侧。

zh.text: 幻想对应点，让相机定位更稳
这种“脑补”能力有什么实际用处？作者把它接到了绝对相机位姿估计上——这是视觉定位里的关键一环。在 ScanNet 留出场景的 2500 对源图/目标图上，他们统计了位姿被正确估计的比例——判定标准是旋转误差 < 20°、平移误差 < 1.5 m——并观察这个比例如何随两张图的视觉重叠度而变化。

zh.caption: 图7 绝对相机位姿实验（ScanNet）。横轴为图像对的最大视觉重叠度，纵轴为位姿被正确估计的比例。绿色曲线是 NeurHal，明显高于所有对比的局部特征匹配方法，尤其是在重叠很少、大多数对应点都不可见的困难区间。

zh.text: 差距最大的地方，恰恰是两张图几乎不重叠、绝大多数对应点都落在视野之外的时候——而 NeurHal 是唯一能“外补”这些点的方法。也就是说，能不能想象出画面之外的对应点，直接决定了低重叠图像对上的定位成败。
到底是哪一项在起作用
那么，三个任务里究竟是谁带来了这份稳健？作者在 ScanNet 上做了一次消融，逐一考察识别、内补、外补各自的贡献。

zh.caption: 图6 消融实验（ScanNet）。深色曲线为同时学习识别、内补、外补三个任务的完整 NeurHal；一旦去掉外补任务（浅色曲线），在低重叠区间的位姿精度明显下降。相比之下，内补任务带来的额外提升要小得多。

zh.text: 结论是：同时训练三个任务效果最好，而真正拉开差距的是外补任务——在低重叠、对应点大多落在视野之外的情形下，它几乎决定了成败；内补任务对相机位姿估计的额外帮助则相当有限。这也和直觉吻合：越是难的低重叠场景，越需要把对应点“想”到画面之外去。
小结与边界
这篇工作给出的信息简单却有力：一个网络可以学会幻想关键点的对应——无论可见、被遮挡，还是完全落在视野之外——而这种幻想能力，让绝对相机位姿估计在低重叠图像对上明显更稳健。换句话说，NeurHal 把“不可见区域”从需要丢弃的噪声，重新定义成可以通过学习几何推理去预测的信号。
当然也要看到它的边界。NeurHal 输出的是刻意保持低分辨率的概率分布，强调的是几何上的合理位置而非像素级精度；外补点的定位仍带有可观的不确定性，往往只是把概率质量压到正确的方位区域。但作为把“脑补对应点”正式变成一个可学习任务的第一步，它已经清楚地证明：让网络去想象看不见的东西，是有价值的。

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 匹配不到，就“脑补”：让网络学会想象看不见的对应点
zh.subtitle: École des Ponts 与波尔多大学提出 NeurHal，把遮挡与视野之外的对应点从“噪声”变成可预测的“信号”

en.text: Which task actually does the work
So which of the three tasks buys this robustness? An ablation on ScanNet isolates the contribution of identifying, inpainting, and outpainting one at a time.

en.caption: Figure 6. Ablation on ScanNet. The dark curve is the full NeurHal trained on all three tasks — identifying, inpainting, and outpainting. Dropping the outpainting task (the lighter curves) clearly lowers pose accuracy in the low-overlap regime, whereas adding inpainting contributes far less.

en.text: The verdict: training on all three tasks together works best, and the outpainting task is what actually opens the gap — in low-overlap scenes, where most correspondents fall outside the frame, it very nearly decides the outcome. Adding inpainting, by contrast, brings only a modest extra benefit to pose estimation. That squares with intuition: the harder the low-overlap case, the more you need to place correspondents beyond the visible image.

zh.text: 到底是哪一项在起作用
那么，三个任务里究竟是谁带来了这份稳健？作者在 ScanNet 上做了一次消融，逐一考察识别、内补、外补各自的贡献。

zh.caption: 图6 消融实验（ScanNet）。深色曲线为同时学习识别、内补、外补三个任务的完整 NeurHal；一旦去掉外补任务（浅色曲线），在低重叠区间的位姿精度明显下降。相比之下，内补任务带来的额外提升要小得多。

zh.text: 结论是：同时训练三个任务效果最好，而真正拉开差距的是外补任务——在低重叠、对应点大多落在视野之外的情形下，它几乎决定了成败；内补任务对相机位姿估计的额外帮助则相当有限。这也和直觉吻合：越是难的低重叠场景，越需要把对应点“想”到画面之外去。

en.title: ICLR 2022: A Network That Hallucinates the Matches It Cannot See
en.subtitle: Germain, Lepetit, and Bourmaud introduce NeurHal, which turns occluded and out-of-frame correspondents from noise to be discarded into signal to be predicted

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 匹配不到，就“脑补”：让网络学会想象看不见的对应点
zh.subtitle: École des Ponts 与波尔多大学提出 NeurHal，把遮挡与视野之外的对应点从“噪声”变成可预测的“信号”

en.text: Establishing correspondences between two overlapping images is a foundational step in computer vision, underpinning everything from visual localization to 3D reconstruction. Yet both classical and deep local-feature matchers share an unspoken assumption: a keypoint can only be “matched” if it is visible in both images. The moment it is hidden behind foreground clutter, or simply falls outside the field of view of the second image, these methods have nothing to say and quietly discard those regions as noise.

That assumption is exactly where things break down. Modern localization leans on keypoint matches, and when two images share little overlap, most points are either occluded or out of frame, so matching collapses. Humans do not give up so easily. Faced with a point they cannot see, people reason about the geometry of the scene and infer where the match ought to be. Classical vision uses geometric reasoning too, but almost always after the fact, wielding models like epipolar geometry to reject bad matches. No prior method actually predicts correspondences at locations that are not covisible across the two views.

This ICLR 2022 paper goes straight at that gap. The authors introduce the task of visual correspondence hallucination, along with a network called NeurHal. Given a pair of overlapping source and target images and a set of keypoints in the source, NeurHal outputs, for every keypoint, a probability distribution over its correspondent’s location in the target image — whether that location is visible, occluded, or entirely beyond the target frame.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three flavors of correspondence hallucination. The top row shows source images with a small set of keypoints; the bottom row shows the probability distributions NeurHal predicts in the target image. A red circle marks a visible correspondent that can simply be identified, a red plus marks an occluded point that must be inpainted, and a red cross marks a point beyond the target’s borders that must be outpainted. All three pairs come from scenes unseen during training.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09711 (arXiv:2106.09711, ICLR 2022). Authors: Hugo Germain, Vincent Lepetit, and Guillaume Bourmaud.
Can it really imagine the match?

The paper’s first research question is whether NeurHal can genuinely hallucinate unseen correspondents on scenes it never trained on. The capability table below gives a qualitative answer — the paper quantifies this with precision curves; here we only ask what each method can and cannot do.

en.caption: Table 1. What NeurHal and mainstream local-feature matchers can do on the three correspondence tasks.

en.text: The pattern is clear. Everyone can identify visible points; on inpainting, methods like LoFTR, DRC-Net, and S2DNet are weak; and on outpainting they fail almost entirely — because they only ever search inside the target’s borders and never place a correspondent beyond the frame. NeurHal, by contrast, produces predictions concentrated near the true location in all three cases. Figure 5 shows this ability directly on image pairs from scenes held out at training time.

en.caption: Figure 5. Qualitative inpainting and outpainting results. The top row shows outpainting examples, the bottom row inpainting examples. Each group runs, left to right: the source image with a keypoint (red dot), the target image, and the (negative-log) correspondence map predicted by NeurHal; the dashed blue rectangle marks the target’s true borders and the red circle marks the ground-truth correspondent. Even when the answer lies outside the frame, the probability mass concentrates on the correct side of the border.

zh.text: 在两张有重叠的图片之间找到对应点，是从视觉定位到三维重建的基础一步。但无论是传统方法还是深度局部特征匹配，都有一个隐含前提：一个关键点只有在两张图里都看得见，才谈得上“匹配”。一旦它被前景挡住，或者干脆落在第二张图的画面之外，这些方法就无话可说，只能把这些区域当作噪声丢掉。
问题在于，现代视觉定位恰恰依赖这些关键点匹配，而当两张图片的重叠很少时，绝大多数点都处于被遮挡或视野之外的状态，匹配随之崩溃。人类却不会就此放弃：面对一个看不见的点，我们会根据场景的几何结构去推断它“应该”落在哪里。经典视觉里当然也有几何推理，但通常只用在事后，用对极几何这类模型去剔除错误匹配，从没有人真正去主动预测那些不可见位置上的对应点。
这篇发表于 ICLR 2022 的论文，正是冲着这个空白去的。作者提出“视觉对应幻想”（visual correspondence hallucination）这一新任务，以及一个名为 NeurHal 的网络：给定一对有重叠的源图与目标图，以及源图中的一批关键点，NeurHal 为每个关键点输出它的对应点在目标图上位置的概率分布——无论这个位置是可见、被遮挡，还是落在视野之外。

zh.caption: 图1 视觉对应幻想的三种情形。上排是源图及其上标出的少量关键点，下排是目标图上 NeurHal 预测的概率分布。红圈表示可以直接识别的可见对应点，红十字为需要“内补”的被遮挡点，红叉为需要“外补”、落在目标图边界之外的点。三组示例都来自训练时未见过的场景。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09711 （arXiv:2106.09711，ICLR 2022）。作者：Hugo Germain、Vincent Lepetit、Guillaume Bourmaud。
当匹配“看不见”时
要理解这项工作，先把对应点的定位拆成三个子任务。作者把它们统一命名为：识别（identifying，对应点在目标图里可见）、内补（inpainting，对应点被前景遮挡）、外补（outpainting，对应点落在目标图视野之外）。传统匹配方法天生只能处理第一种，因为它们只在目标图的像素范围内寻找最相似的描述子：被遮挡的点没有可匹配的外观，视野之外的点根本不在搜索范围里。
NeurHal 的目标，是用同一个网络把这三种情形一并解决。它在室内场景 ScanNet 上训练、并在 NYU Depth 上测试；在室外场景 MegaDepth 上训练、在 ETH-3D 上测试。关键在于，所有评测都使用训练时从未见过的场景，因此结果衡量的是真正的泛化能力，而不是对训练场景的记忆。

en.title: ICLR 2022: A Network That Hallucinates the Matches It Cannot See
en.subtitle: Germain, Lepetit, and Bourmaud introduce NeurHal, which turns occluded and out-of-frame correspondents from noise to be discarded into signal to be predicted

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 匹配不到，就“脑补”：让网络学会想象看不见的对应点
zh.subtitle: École des Ponts 与波尔多大学提出 NeurHal，把遮挡与视野之外的对应点从“噪声”变成可预测的“信号”

en.caption: Figure 1. Three flavors of correspondence hallucination. The top row shows source images with a small set of keypoints; the bottom row shows the probability distributions NeurHal predicts in the target image. A red circle marks a visible correspondent that can simply be identified, a red plus marks an occluded point that must be inpainted, and a red cross marks a point beyond the target’s borders that must be outpainted. All three pairs come from scenes unseen during training.

en.text: When matching runs out of pixels

It helps to break the problem into three sub-tasks, which the authors name explicitly: identifying (the correspondent is visible in the target), inpainting (the correspondent is occluded by foreground), and outpainting (the correspondent lies outside the target’s field of view). Conventional matchers can only ever handle the first, because they search for the most similar descriptor within the target’s pixel grid: an occluded point has no matching appearance, and an out-of-frame point is not even inside the search region.

NeurHal aims to solve all three with a single network. It is trained on the indoor dataset ScanNet and also tested on NYU Depth; outdoors, it is trained on MegaDepth and tested on ETH-3D. Crucially, every evaluation uses scenes never seen during training, so the numbers measure genuine generalization rather than memorization of the training environments.

zh.text: 幻想对应点，让相机定位更稳
这种“脑补”能力有什么实际用处？作者把它接到了绝对相机位姿估计上——这是视觉定位里的关键一环。在 ScanNet 留出场景的 2500 对源图/目标图上，他们统计了位姿被正确估计的比例——判定标准是旋转误差 < 20°、平移误差 < 1.5 m——并观察这个比例如何随两张图的视觉重叠度而变化。

zh.caption: 图7 绝对相机位姿实验（ScanNet）。横轴为图像对的最大视觉重叠度，纵轴为位姿被正确估计的比例。绿色曲线是 NeurHal，明显高于所有对比的局部特征匹配方法，尤其是在重叠很少、大多数对应点都不可见的困难区间。

zh.text: 差距最大的地方，恰恰是两张图几乎不重叠、绝大多数对应点都落在视野之外的时候——而 NeurHal 是唯一能“外补”这些点的方法。也就是说，能不能想象出画面之外的对应点，直接决定了低重叠图像对上的定位成败。

en.title: ICLR 2022: A Network That Hallucinates the Matches It Cannot See
en.subtitle: Germain, Lepetit, and Bourmaud introduce NeurHal, which turns occluded and out-of-frame correspondents from noise to be discarded into signal to be predicted

zh.title: ICLR 2022 | 匹配不到，就“脑补”：让网络学会想象看不见的对应点
zh.subtitle: École des Ponts 与波尔多大学提出 NeurHal，把遮挡与视野之外的对应点从“噪声”变成可预测的“信号”

en.text: How NeurHal hallucinates
The architecture reads left to right in Figure 2, from the two input images to a set of per-keypoint correspondence maps.

en.caption: Figure 2. Overview of NeurHal. On the left, a siamese backbone turns the source and target images into dense descriptor maps (the target map is padded outward with a learnable vector λ). A cross-attention backbone in the middle lets the two communicate, and on the right each keypoint feature is convolved over the target features and passed through a 2D softmax to yield a correspondence map.

en.text: In detail, a siamese convolutional backbone first encodes both images into dense descriptor maps. To give locations beyond the frame something to match against, the target descriptor map is padded outward with a learnable vector λ, effectively initializing descriptors past the image borders. A cross-attention backbone with positional encoding then lets the source and target descriptors exchange information — and this is precisely what allows the network to produce peaked distributions for occluded and out-of-frame points. Finally, each keypoint’s feature is convolved over the target features with a 1×1 convolution and passed through a 2D softmax to produce one correspondence map.

Training simply minimizes a sum of Neural Reprojection Error (NRE) terms — the negative log-likelihood of the true reprojected location — optimized with SGD and early stopping. The procedure assumes nothing about visibility and needs no labels marking points as visible, occluded, or out of frame; the network only ever emits correspondence maps. To emphasize geometry over texture detail, the maps are kept deliberately low-resolution: with an effective stride of 8 and an output ratio γ=50%, a 640×480 target yields a 160×120 map.

The paper’s first research question is whether NeurHal can genuinely hallucinate unseen correspondents on scenes it never trained on. The capability table below gives a qualitative answer — the paper quantifies this with precision curves; here we only ask what each method can and cannot do.

en.caption: Table 1. What NeurHal and mainstream local-feature matchers can do on the three correspondence tasks.

Everyone can identify visible points; on inpainting, methods like LoFTR, DRC-Net, and S2DNet are weak; and on outpainting they fail almost entirely — because they only ever search inside the target’s borders and never place a correspondent beyond the frame. NeurHal, by contrast, produces predictions concentrated near the true location in all three cases. Figure 5 shows this ability directly on image pairs from scenes held out at training time.

en.caption: Figure 5. Qualitative inpainting and outpainting results. The top row shows outpainting examples, the bottom row inpainting examples. Each group runs, left to right: the source image with a keypoint (red dot), the target image, and the (negative-log) correspondence map predicted by NeurHal; the dashed blue rectangle marks the target’s true borders and the red circle marks the ground-truth correspondent. Even when the answer lies outside the frame, the probability mass concentrates on the correct side of the border.

它真的能“想象”出对应点吗
论文的第一个核心问题是：在没见过的场景里，NeurHal 能不能真正幻想出看不见的对应点？下面这张能力对比表先给出一个定性的回答——原文用精度曲线做了量化，这里只关心“能不能做到”。

zh.caption: 表1 NeurHal 与主流局部特征匹配方法在三类对应任务上的能力对比。

zh.text: 结论很直接：在识别可见点上，大家都能做；但在内补上，LoFTR、DRC-Net、S2DNet 等方法表现很弱；而在外补上它们几乎完全失效——因为这些方法只会在目标图边界以内搜索，根本不会把对应点放到画面之外。NeurHal 则在三种情形下都能给出集中在真实位置附近的预测。图5 用几组训练时未见过的图片，把这种能力直观地展示了出来。

zh.caption: 图5 定性的内补/外补结果。上排为外补示例，下排为内补示例。每组从左到右依次是：带关键点（红点）的源图、目标图，以及 NeurHal 预测的（负对数）对应图；蓝色虚线框标出目标图的真实边界，红圈为真实对应点。可以看到，即便正确答案落在边界之外，概率质量也能集中到框外正确的一侧。

zh.text: 小结与边界
这篇工作给出的信息简单却有力：一个网络可以学会幻想关键点的对应——无论可见、被遮挡，还是完全落在视野之外——而这种幻想能力，让绝对相机位姿估计在低重叠图像对上明显更稳健。换句话说，NeurHal 把“不可见区域”从需要丢弃的噪声，重新定义成可以通过学习几何推理去预测的信号。
当然也要看到它的边界。NeurHal 输出的是刻意保持低分辨率的概率分布，强调的是几何上的合理位置而非像素级精度；外补点的定位仍带有可观的不确定性，往往只是把概率质量压到正确的方位区域。但作为把“脑补对应点”正式变成一个可学习任务的第一步，它已经清楚地证明：让网络去想象看不见的东西，是有价值的。

en.text: Takeaway and boundaries

The message is simple but powerful: a single network can learn to hallucinate keypoint correspondences — visible, occluded, or entirely out of frame — and that ability makes absolute camera pose estimation markedly more robust on low-overlap image pairs. Put differently, NeurHal reframes non-covisible regions not as noise to be thrown away but as signal to be predicted through learned geometric reasoning.

It is worth being honest about the limits. NeurHal outputs deliberately low-resolution distributions that favor geometrically plausible location over pixel-level precision, and outpainted points still carry substantial uncertainty — often the model can only push the probability mass to the correct region. But as a first step toward turning correspondence hallucination into a learnable task in its own right, it makes the case cleanly: teaching a network to imagine what it cannot see is worth doing.

zh.text: 它真的能“想象”出对应点吗
论文的第一个核心问题是：在没见过的场景里，NeurHal 能不能真正幻想出看不见的对应点？下面这张能力对比表先给出一个定性的回答——原文用精度曲线做了量化，这里只关心“能不能做到”。

zh.caption: 表1 NeurHal 与主流局部特征匹配方法在三类对应任务上的能力对比。

zh.text: 结论很直接：在识别可见点上，大家都能做；但在内补上，LoFTR、DRC-Net、S2DNet 等方法表现很弱；而在外补上它们几乎完全失效——因为这些方法只会在目标图边界以内搜索，根本不会把对应点放到画面之外。NeurHal 则在三种情形下都能给出集中在真实位置附近的预测。图5 用几组训练时未见过的图片，把这种能力直观地展示了出来。

zh.caption: 图5 定性的内补/外补结果。上排为外补示例，下排为内补示例。每组从左到右依次是：带关键点（红点）的源图、目标图，以及 NeurHal 预测的（负对数）对应图；蓝色虚线框标出目标图的真实边界，红圈为真实对应点。可以看到，即便正确答案落在边界之外，概率质量也能集中到框外正确的一侧。

zh.text: 到底是哪一项在起作用
那么，三个任务里究竟是谁带来了这份稳健？作者在 ScanNet 上做了一次消融，逐一考察识别、内补、外补各自的贡献。

zh.caption: 图6 消融实验（ScanNet）。深色曲线为同时学习识别、内补、外补三个任务的完整 NeurHal；一旦去掉外补任务（浅色曲线），在低重叠区间的位姿精度明显下降。相比之下，内补任务带来的额外提升要小得多。

zh.text: 结论是：同时训练三个任务效果最好，而真正拉开差距的是外补任务——在低重叠、对应点大多落在视野之外的情形下，它几乎决定了成败；内补任务对相机位姿估计的额外帮助则相当有限。这也和直觉吻合：越是难的低重叠场景，越需要把对应点“想”到画面之外去。
